newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE, FIRMER IN SLOW TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE, FIRMER IN SLOW TRADE.

text.p: Short-term interest rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted stable to firmer in thin trade on Tuesday.
Local money dealers said the rates were likely to edge up steadily in January, with liquidity expected to be reduced due to fewer treasury bill maturities.
"Most people are just holding onto to their paper so they can sell at a profit later. Everyone wants to keep their portfolios small at the moment," a dealer commented.

On Tuesday, discount houses were indicating a selling rate of 17.85 percent for treasury bills, slightly up from Monday's 17.80 percent. NCD bills redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days were quoted unchanged at 19.50 and 18.25 percent (buying and selling respectively) while bankers acceptance bills held steady at 18.50 percent (buying) but were being sold firmer at 17.85 from 17.75 percent.
Call money was unmoved from 18 percent in a market which opened with a surplus of Z$40 million.
